scope_note: New Jersey has one statewide construction code, the Uniform Construction Code (N.J.A.C. 5:23), enforced by each municipality's construction office. Everything in fixtures, hdpe_fire and access applies in Newark as in every other municipality; a city agent has no local building or plumbing amendments to look for. The 2024 editions were adopted on August 17, 2026; N.J.A.C. 5:23-1.6 gives applicants six months after a subcode revision to file a complete permit application under the previous code.

governing_table.table: Table 7.21.1, Minimum Number of Required Plumbing Fixtures (Section 7.21)
governing_table.quote: 7.21.1 Number of Fixtures. Plumbing fixtures shall be provided for the type of building occupancy and in the numbers not less than those shown in Table 7.21.1.
governing_table.adoption_quote: the Commissioner hereby adopts the Model Code of the International Association of Plumbing and Mechanical Officials, known as "The National Standard Plumbing Code/2024," as the plumbing subcode for New Jersey. | [Building subcode, N.J.A.C. 5:23-3.14(b)] 20. Chapters 28, Mechanical Systems, and 29, Plumbing Systems, shall be deleted in their [entirety]
governing_table.note: Read in IAPMO's free read-only edition of the 2024 National Standard Plumbing Code Illustrated, New Jersey Edition (linked from iapmo.org; a page-image reader whose page text was read from the reader's own search index, pages 122 to 130 and 279 to 281 of the file, printed pages 110 to 118 and 267 to 269). The building subcode deletes Chapter 29 of the 2024 International Building Code, so the IBC's Table 2902.1 does not apply in New Jersey. New Jersey's amendments to Section 7.21 (N.J.A.C. 5:23-3.15(b)7) change 'building code' to 'building subcode' in 7.21.2.b and 7.21.9, delete 7.21.10 (adult changing station), rename the R-2 dwelling row and delete the second sentence of table note 1; none changes the business, restaurant or school rows.

fixtures.cities_may_amend_note: The State Uniform Construction Code Act makes the code uniform: municipal construction regulations were repealed and superseded when the state code was promulgated (N.J.S.A. 52:27D-139: 'All construction regulations incorporated in any act of the State of New Jersey, or of any municipality presently in effect ... shall continue in effect until such time as any such regulation is superseded by appropriate regulations promulgated pursuant to this act, at which time they shall be deemed repealed and superseded, and of no further force and effect.'). Municipalities enforce the code; they do not amend it. https://www.nj.gov/dca/codes/codreg/pdf_regs/52_27D_119.pdf

sex_split.text: The number of people each restroom serves is set by the designer of the plumbing system. Where both sexes are present in about equal numbers, half are counted as male and half as female, unless specific information on the split is available. For all-gender toilet facilities the count is the sum of the men's and women's counts.
sex_split.quote: 7.21.2 Occupant Load a. The minimum number of plumbing fixtures shall be based on the number of persons to be served by the fixtures, as determined by the person responsible for the design of the plumbing system. ... c. Wherever both sexes are present in approximately equal numbers, the total occupant load shall be multiplied by 50 percent to determine the number of persons of each sex to be provided for, unless specific information concerning the percentage of male and female occupants is available. ... f. For all gender toilet facilities, the minimum number of fixtures shall be the aggregate calculated at 50 percent female and 50 percent male in accordance with Table 7.21.1. Where all gender plumbing fixtures are provided in addition to separate men's and women's facilities, those all gender plumbing fixtures shall be included in determining the number of fixtures provided in an occupancy.

rounding.text: Part of a listed group counts as a whole group, so fractions round up. Where two occupancy types share the same fixtures, the fractions are added first and then rounded up.
rounding.quote: Note (16) In determining the number of required fixtures for numbers of persons that fall in the "each additional (xx) over (xx)" listings, the requirement applies to fractions of the listed group (7.21.10). | 7.21.13 Fractions of the Minimum Number of Required Plumbing Fixtures a. In Table 7.21.1, where the number of persons of each sex is less than 100% of a particular group, the number of fixtures required for that group may be reduced by the fraction of the persons in that group. The fraction of the required fixtures shall be rounded up to the next whole number. b. Where a facility includes two or more different occupancy classifications with access to the same installed plumbing fixtures, the fraction of the required fixtures for each classification may be added and the total combined fraction of the required fixtures shall be rounded up to the next whole number. | Appendix D, Example B: 'for each group of 50 over 50 (or parts thereof) add 1 water closet'

urinal_substitution.text: Urinals are optional. In a men's toilet room they may replace up to 50% of the required water closets, in every occupancy. The code's own worked example turns 5 required water closets into 3 water closets and 2 urinals, and 6 into 3 and 3.
urinal_substitution.quote: 7.21.5 Substitution and Omission of Fixtures a. Urinals: In male toilet rooms, urinals may be substituted for up to 50% of the required number of water closets. | Table note (5) Not more than 50% of the required number of water closets for males may be urinals (7.21.5.a). | Appendix D, Example B: 'The minimum number of water closets required for males = 5. Section 7.21.5a permits 50% of the required water closets for males to be urinals. The male toilet room could contain 3 water closets and 2 urinals.'

small_occupancy_exception.text: Separate men's and women's rooms are not required: in occupancies serving 15 or fewer people (one single-user room for both sexes); in business occupancies of 1,500 square feet or less and mercantile occupancies with 1,500 square feet or less open to customers (one single-user room serves customers and employees); or where a room is designed for use by both sexes with every water closet in a privacy compartment and urinals visually separated or in compartments. A restaurant with a seated load over 100 customers needs separate employee toilets.
small_occupancy_exception.quote: 7.21.4 Separate Facilities a. Separate toilet facilities shall be provided for each sex. EXCEPTIONS: (1) Residential installations. (2) In occupancies serving 15 or fewer people, one toilet facility, designed for use by no more than one person at a time, shall be permitted for use by both sexes. (3) In business occupancies with a total floor area of 1500 square feet or less, one toilet facility, designed for use by no more than one person at a time, shall satisfy the requirements for serving customers and employees of both sexes. (4) In mercantile occupancies with a net occupiable floor area of 1500 square feet or less that is accessible to customers, one toilet facility designed for use by no more than one person at a time shall satisfy the requirements for serving customers and employees of both sexes. (5) Separate facilities shall not be required where rooms have fixtures designed for use by both sexes and the water closets are installed in privacy compartments. Urinals shall be located in an area that is visually separated from the remainder of the room or each urinal shall be installed in a privacy compartment. | 7.21.8 Food Service Establishments a. Restaurants and other food service establishments with a seated occupant load exceeding 100 customers shall be provided with separate toilet facilities for employees and customers. Customer and employee toilet facilities may be combined for seated customer loads of 100 or less and fixtures shall be provided for the total number of customers and employees. For employees of 15 or less, one employee toilet facility, designed for use by no more than one person at a time, shall be permitted for use by both sexes.

occupant_load.text: The plumbing count uses the number of people to be served, set by the designer. Where that number is not established and is taken from the building subcode's egress occupant load, it may be reduced to two thirds. In a restaurant or other space with established seating it may not be less than the number of seats. The building subcode's egress table (2024 IBC Table 1004.5, New Jersey edition) counts business areas at 150 gross square feet per occupant, assembly without fixed seats, unconcentrated (tables and chairs) at 15 net, and educational classroom area at 20 net. New Jersey's amendments to Table 1004.5 touch only the swimming pool rows.
occupant_load.quote: 7.21.2 b. Where the occupant load is not established and is based on the egress requirements of a building subcode, the number of occupants for plumbing purposes shall be permitted to be reduced to two-thirds of that for fire or life safety purposes. ... e. In occupancies having established seating, such as auditoriums and restaurants, the number of occupants for plumbing purposes shall not be less than the number of seats. | Table 1004.5: 'Assembly without fixed seats ... Unconcentrated (tables and chairs) 15 net' | 'Business areas 150 gross' | 'Educational Classroom area 20 net'
occupant_load.note: Table 1004.5 was read on UpCodes' copy of the New Jersey UCC Building Subcode 2024 (secondary). The official amendment list, N.J.A.C. 5:23-3.14(b)9iii, changes only the swimming pool and deck rows of that table.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: The 'occupants' figure is the number of people served for plumbing purposes (Section 7.21.2.a). If a project starts from the egress occupant load, Section 7.21.2.b lets the designer use two thirds of it before applying the table, which lowers these counts. School examples use row E-2 (grades 1 to 6); row E-3 (grades 7 to 12) is given alongside in each school example. Row E-1 (day care, preschool, kindergarten) is stricter: 15 or less: 1; 16 - 30: add 1; 31 - 50: add 1; 51 - 75: add 1; 76 - 100: add 1; each additional 50 over 100: add 1.

hdpe_fire.section: 2024 International Building Code, New Jersey edition (building subcode, N.J.A.C. 5:23-3.14), Section 803.9, with Section 803.1.1 and the Chapter 2 definition of Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish
hdpe_fire.quote: 803.9 High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) and Polypropylene (PP). Where high-density polyethylene or polypropylene is used as an interior finish, it shall comply with Section 803.1.1. | 803.1.1 Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish Materials Tested in Accordance With NFPA 286. Interior wall and ceiling finish materials shall be classified in accordance with NFPA 286 and comply with Section 803.1.1.1. Materials complying with Section 803.1.1.1 shall be considered to also comply with the requirements of Class A. | Chapter 2: [BF] Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish. The exposed interior surfaces of buildings, including but not limited to: fixed or movable walls and partitions; toilet room privacy partitions; columns; ceilings; and interior wainscoting, paneling or other finish applied structurally or for decoration, acoustical correction, surface insulation, structural fire resistance or similar purposes, but not including trim.
hdpe_fire.note: Section text read on UpCodes' copy of the New Jersey UCC Building Subcode 2024 (secondary). The official amendment list in N.J.A.C. 5:23-3.14(b) (read on nj.gov) goes from Chapter 7 straight to Chapter 9, so Chapter 8 is adopted without change, and its Chapter 2 amendments were not seen to touch this definition. For work in existing buildings the Rehabilitation Subcode (N.J.A.C. 5:23-6) decides which requirements for new materials apply; that was not traced for interior finish.

access.state_standard: New Jersey Barrier Free Subcode: Chapter 11 of the 2024 International Building Code as amended at N.J.A.C. 5:23-3.14(b)10, with ICC A117.1-2017 (the state's current-codes page lists 'ICC A117.1-2017 w/ supp') as the technical standard, also amended there; N.J.A.C. 5:23-7 now covers recreation only ('The accessibility regulations, other than recreation, shall be found in Chapter 11 of the building subcode, as amended at N.J.A.C. 5:23-3.14(b).'). New Jersey's amendments to A117.1 delete its Chapter 2 scoping and Sections 607.8 and 608.8 (water temperature) and change other items; none seen changes Sections 603 or 604 on toilet rooms and compartments.

differences.point: Vertical grab bar beside the toilet
differences.state: ICC A117.1-2017, 604.5.1: 'Fixed side-wall grab bars shall include a horizontal bar complying with Section 604.5.1.1 and a vertical grab bar complying with Section 604.5.1.2.' 604.5.1.2: 'A vertical grab bar 18 inches (455 mm) minimum in length shall be mounted with the bottom of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum above the floor, and with the center line of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum from the rear wall.' Ambulatory stalls need side-wall grab bars, vertical bar included, on both sides (604.10.4).
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 604.5.1: 'The side wall grab bar shall be 42 inches (1065 mm) long minimum, located 12 inches (305 mm) maximum from the rear wall and extending 54 inches (1370 mm) minimum from the rear wall.' No vertical grab bar is required.
differences.quote: A vertical grab bar 18 inches (455 mm) minimum in length shall be mounted with the bottom of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum above the floor

differences.point: Toe clearance under the wheelchair stall's partitions
differences.state: ICC A117.1-2017, 604.9.5.1: 'The front partition and at least one side partition of wheelchair accessible toilet compartments shall provide a toe clearance of 12 inches (305 mm) minimum above the floor and extending 8 inches (205 mm) beyond the compartment side face of the partition, exclusive of partition support members. Exceptions: Toe clearance at the front partition is not required in a wheelchair accessible toilet compartment greater than 64 inches (1625 mm) in depth with a wall-hung water closet, or greater than 67 inches (1700 mm) in depth with a floor-mounted water closet. Toe clearance at the side partition is not required in a wheelchair accessible toilet compartment greater than 68 inches (1725 mm) in width.'
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 604.8.1.4: 'The front partition and at least one side partition shall provide a toe clearance of 9 inches (230 mm) minimum above the finish floor and 6 inches (150 mm) deep minimum beyond the compartment-side face of the partition, exclusive of partition support members. Compartments for children's use shall provide a toe clearance of 12 inches (305 mm) minimum above the finish floor. EXCEPTION: Toe clearance at the front partition is not required in a compartment greater than 62 inches (1575 mm) deep with a wall-hung water closet or 65 inches (1650 mm) deep with a floor-mounted water closet. Toe clearance at the side partition is not required in a compartment greater than 66 inc[hes wide]'
differences.quote: a toe clearance of 12 inches (305 mm) minimum above the floor and extending 8 inches (205 mm) beyond the compartment side face of the partition

differences.state: 2024 IBC (NJ edition) 1110.2.4: 'Where water closet compartments are provided in a toilet room or bathing room, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be wheelchair accessible. Where the combined total water closet compartments and urinals provided in a toilet room or bathing room is six or more, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be ambulatory accessible, provided in addition to the wheelchair-accessible compartment.'
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 213.3.1: 'Where toilet compartments are provided, at least one toilet compartment shall comply with 604.8.1. In addition to the compartment required to comply with 604.8.1, at least one compartment shall comply with 604.8.2 where six or more toilet compartments are provided, or where the combination of urinals and water closets totals six or more fixtures.'
differences.quote: at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be wheelchair accessible
differences.note: The two give the same answer until a room has more than 20 compartments.

differences.point: Family or assisted-use toilet room in restaurants, other assembly buildings and stores
differences.state: 2024 IBC (NJ edition) 1110.2.1: 'In assembly and mercantile occupancies, an accessible family or assisted-use toilet room shall be provided where an aggregate of six or more male and female water closets is required.' The plumbing subcode (7.21.9) lets its fixtures count toward the men's or women's minimum in those occupancies.
differences.federal: The 2010 ADA Standards have no requirement to provide a family or assisted-use toilet room; 213.2 only permits a unisex room in place of altering existing rooms where full compliance is technically infeasible.
differences.quote: an accessible family or assisted-use toilet room shall be provided where an aggregate of six or more male and female water closets is required

differences.point: Installing or moving partitions in an existing restroom triggers an accessible stall
differences.state: Rehabilitation Subcode, N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.5(e)2 (renovations; the same text appears for alterations and reconstruction): 'In buildings required by Chapter 11 of the building subcode to be accessible, when bathrooms or toilet rooms are renovated, the following requirements for providing accessibility shall apply unless the requirements of Chapter 11 of the building subcode have been met: i. When toilet partitions are moved or installed, but existing fixtures are not being moved, an accessible stall complying with ICC A117.1, Section 604.9 shall be created provided that this can be accomplished without moving fixtures. (Building) ... iii. Where full compliance is technically infeasible, compliance shall be achieved to the maximum extent feasible.'
differences.federal: The 2010 ADA Standards apply to altered elements under their general alteration rule (section 202.3); they have no provision written for toilet partition replacement.
differences.quote: When toilet partitions are moved or installed, but existing fixtures are not being moved, an accessible stall complying with ICC A117.1, Section 604.9 shall be created provided that this can be accomplished without moving fixtures.

access.same_as_federal: Read and found the same in both: wheelchair stall 60 inches wide and 56 inches deep with a wall-hung toilet or 59 with a floor-mounted one; ambulatory stall 35 to 37 inches wide and 60 deep; self-closing door with a pull on both sides near the latch; children's wheelchair stall 59 inches deep.
access.process: No separate state registration or review for accessibility. The Barrier Free Subcode is part of the Uniform Construction Code, so the municipal construction office checks it in plan review and inspection with the construction permit (the Rehabilitation Subcode tags the partition rule '(Building)', the building subcode official). Related statewide permit rule read in passing: N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.17A(c)1iii lists as minor work the 'Repair or replacement with no reconfiguration of space of any non-structural component such as a partition in structures other than one- and two-family dwellings'; minor work may start on notice to the enforcing agency, with a permit application filed within five business days. Whether a toilet partition replacement is handled as minor work is for the local construction office to say.

single_user.rule: No statewide requirement was found that single-user restrooms be open to all genders or carry an all-gender sign. The building subcode deletes Chapter 29 of the 2024 IBC, which is where the model code's single-user signage section sits, and the New Jersey edition of the plumbing code has no such section (its text was searched for 'single-user', 'single occupant', 'all gender' and 'signage'). The plumbing code lets one single-user room serve both sexes in small occupancies (15 or fewer people; business or mercantile spaces of 1,500 square feet or less), and exempts single-occupant rooms with a lockable door from the compartment requirement.
single_user.quote: 7.21.4 EXCEPTIONS: ... (2) In occupancies serving 15 or fewer people, one toilet facility, designed for use by no more than one person at a time, shall be permitted for use by both sexes. | 7.21.11 EXCEPTIONS: (1) Water closet compartments shall not be required in a single-occupant toilet room having a lockable door. | N.J.A.C. 5:23-3.14(b)20: 'Chapters 28, Mechanical Systems, and 29, Plumbing Systems, shall be deleted in their [entirety]'

all_gender_shared.rule: Allowed. Separate men's and women's rooms are not required where a room's fixtures are designed for use by both sexes, every water closet is in a privacy compartment, and urinals are visually separated from the rest of the room or each is in a privacy compartment. In an all-gender room, water closet partitions must meet the Type A security requirements of IAPMO/ANSI Z124.10 (2022); in separate men's and women's rooms they must meet Type B, and urinal partitions Type C. The fixture count is the sum of the men's and women's counts.
all_gender_shared.quote: 7.21.4 EXCEPTIONS: ... (5) Separate facilities shall not be required where rooms have fixtures designed for use by both sexes and the water closets are installed in privacy compartments. Urinals shall be located in an area that is visually separated from the remainder of the room or each urinal shall be installed in a privacy compartment. | 7.21.11 Water Closet Compartment. Public water closets shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy. Partitions for water closets located in separate gender toilet or bathrooms shall comply with the Type B security requirements of IAPMO/ANSI Z124.10. Partitions for water closets located in all gender toilet or bathrooms shall comply with the Type A security requirements of IAPMO/ANSI Z124.10. | 7.21.12 Urinal Partitions. Each urinal shall be separated with walls or partitions to provide privacy. The horizontal dimension between walls or partitions at each urinal shall comply with Section 7.3.2. Partitions for urinals shall comply with the Type C security requirements of IAPMO/ANSI Z124.10. Urinals located in all gender toilet rooms shall be visually separated from the remainder of the room or each urinal shall be installed in a privacy compartment complying with Type A security requirements of IAPMO/ANSI Z124.10. EXCEPTION: Urinal partitions shall not be required in a single occupant or family/assisted-use toilet room with a lockable door.
all_gender_shared.note: The building subcode deletes IBC Sections 1210.3, 1210.3.1 and 1210.3.2 (privacy, water closet compartment, urinal partitions), so these plumbing code sections are the compartment rule in New Jersey. What Types A, B and C of IAPMO/ANSI Z124.10 require (gaps, heights, sightlines) was not read: the standard is sold by IAPMO.

use_restrictions.rule: No state law restricting restroom use by sex in particular buildings was found. The Law Against Discrimination lets a place of public accommodation that is by nature restricted to one sex stay so, provided people are admitted based on their gender identity or expression; the Division on Civil Rights states that transgender people must be permitted to use the bathroom consistent with their gender identity or expression.
use_restrictions.quote: N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(f)(1): 'nothing contained herein shall be construed to bar any place of public accommodation which is in its nature reasonably restricted exclusively to individuals of one sex, and which shall include but not be limited to any summer camp, day camp, or resort camp, bathhouse, dressing room, swimming pool, gymnasium, comfort station, dispensary, clinic or hospital, or school or educational institution which is restricted exclusively to individuals of one sex, provided individuals shall be admitted based on their gender identity or expression, from refusing, withholding from or denying to any individual of the opposite sex any of the accommodations, advantages, facilities or privileges thereof on the basis of sex' | Division on Civil Rights fact sheet: 'The LAD requires that individuals be treated consistent with their gender identity. Among other things, transgender people must be permitted to use the bathroom or changing room consistent with their gender identity or expression.'
use_restrictions.note: LAD text read in the Division on Civil Rights' courtesy copy, current through 10/18/2024 (the Division states it is an unofficial copy). Laws passed after that date were not checked on the Legislature's site.

public_wage.law: New Jersey Prevailing Wage Act, N.J.S.A. 34:11-56.25 et seq. The Commissioner of Labor and Workforce Development sets the rates (34:11-56.30), by county and by craft. Contractors and subcontractors on covered public work must register under the Public Works Contractor Registration Act, N.J.S.A. 34:11-56.48 et seq.
public_wage.threshold: $19,375 for contracts awarded directly by municipal government (effective July 1, 2024); $2,000 for every other public body, including boards of education and municipal utility authorities.
public_wage.quote: Public works projects subject to the Act are those funded in whole or in part with the funds of a public body. Contracts awarded directly by municipal government must be valued at $19,375 or more to be covered by the Act. For all other public entities, including municipal utility authorities and boards of education, the threshold is $2,000. | N.J.S.A. 34:11-56.27: 'Every contract in excess of the prevailing wage contract threshold amount for any public work to which any public body is a party or for public work to be done on property or premises owned by a public body or leased or to be leased by a public body shall contain a provision stating the prevailing wage rate which can be paid (as shall be designated by the commissioner) to the workers employed in the performance of the contract' | 34:11-56.30: 'The commissioner shall determine the prevailing wage rate and forthwith shall establish the prevailing wage in the locality in which the public work is to be performed for each craft or trade or classification of all workmen needed to perform public work contracts.'
public_wage.note: The Department's page says rates 'vary by county and by the type of work performed' and are 'based on the collective bargaining agreements established for a particular craft or trade in the locality'. The Essex County carpenter rate for Newark is for the city agent (rate determinations are linked from the rates_url page).

shipped_goods.rule: Taxable. Tax is due to the state where the purchaser takes delivery. A remote seller with no physical presence must register and collect New Jersey tax once its gross revenue from sales delivered into New Jersey exceeds $100,000, or it makes 200 or more separate transactions, in the current or prior calendar year. If the seller does not collect, the purchaser owes use tax at 6.625% on the price, delivery charges included.
shipped_goods.quote: Use Tax is due when taxable tangible personal property, specified digital products, or services are purchased for use in New Jersey but Sales Tax is not collected, or is collected at a rate less than New Jersey's rate. This commonly happens when purchases are made online, by phone or mail order, or outside the State. If the items are delivered to a New Jersey address, the purchaser must pay Use Tax based on the purchase price, including any delivery/shipping charges. The Use Tax rate is the same as the Sales Tax rate, which is 6.625%. | Remote sellers page: '[gross revenue from sales of] tangible personal property, specified digital products, or taxable services delivered into New Jersey during the current or prior calendar year, exceeds $100,000; or The remote seller sold tangible personal property, specified digital products, or taxable services delivered into New Jersey in 200 or more separate transactions during the current or prior calendar year.' | ANJ-10: 'In general, Sales Tax is due to the state where the purchaser takes possession or delivery of the item(s) purchased.'

sales_tax.freight_quote: Delivery Charges for Taxable Property and Services. Sales Tax is imposed on the charges for delivery of property (or services) from a seller directly to a customer if the items sold are subject to tax. ... Delivery charges are defined as charges by the seller for preparation and delivery to a location designated by the purchaser of personal property or services including, but not limited to, transportation, shipping, postage, handling, crating, and packing. (Tax Topic Bulletin S&U-4)

install_labor.rule: Depends on what the work is. Labor that results in an exempt capital improvement (an installation permanently attached to the real property that increases its capital value or useful life) is not taxed, and the property owner gives the contractor a completed Certificate of Exempt Capital Improvement, Form ST-8. Labor for a repair, maintenance or installation service, or for a taxable capital improvement, is taxed. The bulletin's example lists do not name toilet partitions.
install_labor.quote: Capital improvement means an installation of tangible personal property that increases the capital value or useful life of the real property (land or buildings). The item(s) installed must be permanently attached to the real property. Capital improvements are exempt from tax with the exception of those listed under Taxable capital improvements. | Exempt Capital Improvement Services. If the work results in an exempt capital improvement to real property, the contractor does not charge Sales Tax on the bill, regardless of whether the materials and the labor are separately itemized or billed as one amount. The property owner must issue the contractor a fully completed Certificate of Exempt Capital Improvement (Form ST-8). | Whether or not Sales Tax is charged on the customer's bill depends on whether the work is an exempt capital improvement or a taxable capital improvement, repair, maintenance, or installation service. | Real property means land and buildings and any property permanently attached to the land and/or buildings in such a way that its removal would result in substantial damage to the real property.

furnish_and_install.rule: The contractor is the consumer of the materials and pays sales or use tax on them when buying, with no resale treatment. On an exempt capital improvement the contractor charges the owner no tax, whether materials and labor are itemized or not (Form ST-8 on file). On a taxable job, if materials and labor are itemized, only the separately stated pass-through of the actual cost of materials is deducted and the rest is taxed as labor; if not itemized, the whole receipt is taxed. Work on property of the State, its agencies or political subdivisions, federal agencies and exempt nonprofits is exempt for both materials and labor with the right certificate (Form ST-13 for the contractor's purchases). Separate rules apply to fabricator/contractors, who manufacture, sell and install items that become part of real property.
furnish_and_install.quote: For New Jersey Sales Tax purposes, a contractor is considered the actual consumer of the materials and supplies used in construction or in improving, altering, or repairing the real property of others. Sales of materials and supplies to contractors are considered retail sales and, therefore, taxable. | Under the law, a contractor is not granted resale treatment for materials and supplies purchased for improving, altering, or repairing real property. | If the contractor chooses to separately itemize materials and labor on the customer's bill and the bill is for a taxable capital improvement, repair, maintenance, or installation service, the only amount deductible from the receipt for Sales Tax purposes is the separately stated pass-through of the actual cost of materials. ... The remainder of the customer's bill is for labor and is subject to Sales Tax. If the contractor does not itemize the materials and the labor for a taxable job, the entire receipt is subject to tax. | If a contractor purchases materials out of state for use in New Jersey and pays no Sales Tax, or pays tax at a rate less than the current New Jersey Sales Tax rate, the contractor must pay Use Tax to New Jersey on the cost of the materials

sales_tax.note: Tax Topic Bulletin S&U-3, Contractors and New Jersey Taxes, is dated Rev. 5/25; S&U-4, New Jersey Sales Tax Guide, Rev. 07/22. S&U-3 names Urban Enterprise Zones, where qualified businesses have exemptions; whether a reduced rate or an exemption applies at a Newark address is for the city agent. No statement on local sales taxes was read.

page.stalls_intro: New Jersey's rules count toilets by the number of people a restroom serves, a figure the building's designer sets. Where it is taken from the building's capacity (the most people it is designed to hold, worked out from its floor area), the rules allow two thirds of that capacity to be used. Half are counted as men and half as women, and part of a group counts as a whole one. Every toilet needs its own stall with a door. Urinals are optional: in a men's room they can replace up to half of the toilets, and each urinal needs a privacy screen.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building, for the number of people served. The school column is for grades 1 to 6: grades 7 to 12 need 3 stalls for each sex at 200 students and 5 at 400, and kindergartens and day care need more. A space serving 15 people or fewer, or an office of 1,500 square feet or less, can use one single-user restroom for everyone. A restaurant that seats more than 100 customers needs separate toilets for staff.
page.capacity: To find a building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room with tables and chairs at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20, and a restaurant is never counted below its number of seats.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** New Jersey's building rules treat toilet partitions as an interior wall finish and require solid plastic (HDPE) and polypropylene partitions to pass a room-corner fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Federal law and New Jersey's own access rules set the sizes. In an existing building that has to be accessible, installing or moving partitions means creating a wheelchair-accessible stall where that can be done without moving the toilets. There is no separate state review: the local construction office checks access with the construction permit.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **New Jersey extras:** stall sizes match the federal ones, but New Jersey adds a vertical grab bar, 18 inches or longer, on the side wall beside each accessible toilet. The open space under the wheelchair stall's front and side partitions must be 12 inches high and reach 8 inches past the partition, where federal rules ask for 9 and 6. The state's plumbing rules also name a partition standard that stalls and urinal screens must meet, with a higher privacy level for all-gender rooms. A restaurant or store that needs six or more toilets in total must also have a family restroom.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** New Jersey's statewide building rules set no sign requirement for one-person restrooms, so ask the local construction office what it expects. A shared all-gender room is allowed if every toilet sits in a privacy compartment and urinals are screened from the rest of the room or placed in compartments of their own. State civil rights law requires that people be allowed to use the restroom that matches their gender identity.
page.public_jobs: On public work, New Jersey law requires at least the prevailing wage for the trade on contracts of $2,000 or more, or $19,375 or more where a municipal government awards the contract directly; the state Department of Labor and Workforce Development sets the rates by county, and contractors on these jobs must be registered with it.
page.tax_install_bullet: - **Tax on installation:** in New Jersey, installation that counts as a capital improvement to the building (permanently attached, and adding to its value or useful life) is not taxed, and the owner gives the contractor a completed Form ST-8. Repair, maintenance and other installation labor is taxed. The state's lists of examples don't name toilet partitions.
page.tax_ship_bullet: - **Buying without installation:** partitions shipped to {city} are taxed at New Jersey's 6.625% rate, delivery charges included. If the seller doesn't collect the tax, the buyer owes it to the state as use tax.
page.tax_confirm: your accountant or the New Jersey Division of Taxation

page.official_names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; New Jersey Barrier Free Subcode (Chapter 11 of the 2024 International Building Code, New Jersey edition, with ICC A117.1-2017 and supplement; N.J.A.C. 5:23-7); New Jersey Uniform Construction Code (N.J.A.C. 5:23): Building Subcode (2024 International Building Code, New Jersey edition), Plumbing Subcode (2024 National Standard Plumbing Code, New Jersey edition) and Rehabilitation Subcode (N.J.A.C. 5:23-6), 2024 editions adopted August 17, 2026; IAPMO/ANSI Z124.10-2022 for partitions; NFPA 286 for HDPE.

notes: Unusual for partition buyers: the New Jersey plumbing subcode (2024 NSPC Sections 7.21.11 and 7.21.12) requires water closet and urinal partitions to comply with IAPMO/ANSI Z124.10 (listed in the code's standards chapter as 'IAPMO/ANSI Z124.10 - 2022 Water Closet and Urinal Partitions'): Type B for separate-sex rooms, Type A for all-gender rooms, Type C for urinal partitions. Next Partitions should ask its manufacturers which products are certified to which type.

New Jersey uses the National Standard Plumbing Code, not the International Plumbing Code, so its table differs from most states: the business row gives 2 water closets per sex from 16 people of a sex, the urinal limit is 50% in every occupancy, and the plumbing population may be two thirds of the egress occupant load.

Known only from news reports (kept out of page text): a web search surfaced reports of local single-occupancy all-gender restroom measures in Bloomfield Township (ordinance, 2026) and Hoboken (2018 mayoral order), and an unenacted state bill (A4549, 2018-2019 session). None was read on an official page. Newark was not checked; city agent.

IAPMO's 2027 NSPC proposed-changes monograph (August 2025) quotes the current 2024 text of Sections 7.21.2, 7.21.4, 7.21.11 and 7.21.12 and table note 5, and matches the New Jersey edition read here. It proposes for 2027: 'all-gender' wording in 7.21.4(5), a one-for-one water closet for urinal substitution in all-gender rooms, and a note classifying assembly uses under 50 persons as business for fixture counts. Not law.

Permit question, statewide: N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.17A treats 'repair or replacement with no reconfiguration of space of any non-structural component such as a partition' in non-residential buildings as minor work (notice before work, permit application within five business days). The ordinary maintenance list in N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 was not read in full for toilet partitions.
